name: Corporate office
purpose: workplace behaviour, feedback, meetings, policy, onboarding, wellbeing, hybrid work

identity.place: The fourth floor of a converted 1920s brick textile mill in a temperate city, now the head office of a 180-person insurance and operations company. One long open floor about 60 m by 18 m inside, about 4.2 m from floor to the underside of the joists (an old spinning floor, much taller than a modern office), with rooms built inside it as glass and birch-ply boxes.
architecture: white-painted brick walls with the courses still visible; one end wall left as bare red-brown brick
a regular grid of black steel columns, two rows, about 6.7 m apart along the floor and 4.7 m across the bays, with riveted caps; dark timber beams and joists overhead
exposed services hung below the joists, never a suspended ceiling: sprinkler pipes painted dark red with small sprinkler heads, cable trays, round ducts, linear pendant lights

tall steel-sash factory windows in a long regular row on the south wall: each about 1.8 m wide and 2.1 m high, 20 small panes (5 across, 4 high) in thin dark-green-painted steel bars, one centre-pivoting hopper pane per window, a deep concrete sill at about 0.9 m
the original floor: wide sanded maple boards, patched where machines once stood, with flat-weave rugs marking zones

rooms built inside the floor are boxes of birch-ply frame and glass that rise to the joists on a slim steel head track (the joists, the sprinkler pipe and the cable trays run on above them); glass walls run past the columns without touching them; every glass wall carries two frosted manifestation bands, at about 0.9 m and 1.5 m above the floor (plain bands, no words or logos)
identity.materials: birch ply and oak furniture, black powder-coated steel, white and bare brick, sanded maple boards, felt and wool upholstery in slate blue and oat, brass lamp fittings, deep green as the company's colour (a painted wall, felt panels), with signal red only on the few things that are red in life (the sprinkler pipe, a fire extinguisher)
inhabited: work in progress everywhere: printed charts pinned up (empty slots, no text), sticky notes in clusters, archive boxes, labelled trays (no letters)
personal things: a cardigan on a chair back, mismatched mugs, a framed photo turned to face the desk, a small cactus
infrastructure of a real office: cable trays and floor boxes, monitor arms, a first-aid box, a fire extinguisher by a column, coat hooks, an umbrella stand
slight wear: scuffs on the floor along the walking line, a rug corner turned up, a chair with a lower back than the others
identity.default_light: Mid-afternoon in late autumn: low sun from the south windows throws long patches of warm light, broken by the 20-pane grid, across the floor and furniture; daylight away from the windows reads slightly cool and blue; the deep side of the floor is lit by warm linear pendants.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one place (each scene names the ones its camera can see): the 20-pane steel window and its light pattern, a black steel column, white and bare brick, birch-ply joinery, the exposed dark red sprinkler pipe and cable tray, one deep green element, one brass lamp or fitting.
avoid: a generic glass-tower office with no character
real brands, logos, signs with words, flags or anything that pins a country
people in the sets (the cast is separate)
a catalogue-clean room: every scene shows someone works here
windows with a few huge panes or modern casements
screens that face a window or sit with a window right behind them (glare): screens sit at about 90 degrees to the windows
columns at uneven spacing, or columns standing inside a glass wall
a low or tiled ceiling anywhere: the floor is 4.2 m high with exposed services, and the rooms built inside it rise to the joists
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall: the ceiling joists are at 2.4 times a person's height; a door is 2.1 m high and about 0.9 m wide
desk tops at 0.73 m, kitchen worktops at 0.9 m, a standing reception counter at about 1.05 m, a seat at 0.45 m
desks are 1.6 m by 0.8 m per person; four make a back-to-back cluster of 3.2 m by 1.6 m; main walkways about 1.5 m wide
a wall screen in a meeting room is a 65 to 75 inch screen (about 1.5 m wide) with its centre about 1.3 m above the floor

a fire extinguisher hangs on a bracket with its handle about 1 m above the floor; green exit signs with a running figure and an arrow (no words) sit above exit doors, 2.2 to 2.4 m up, above the door head
identity.outside: The view through the windows: low brick terraces, slate roofs, one chimney stack, a few bare trees, a pale sky; no landmarks, no signs.

scenes.light: Main set: early afternoon in late autumn (this set's own time, earlier than the world's default), sun about 25 degrees high from the south-south-west. The screen is OFF (screen tones): the darkest shape in the frame, against the brick and the green felt, with only a soft pale sheen along its right edge. This room is about 5 m deep, so the far layer's haze is 0.1 at most, and the wall_screen group is drawn after the far layer's lm-atmos group so it is not hazed; the near chair back may be as dark as the screen, never darker.
